description: Read Birmingham's civic centre through a war memorial, Pre-Raphaelite art and Burne-Jones glass before Sleeping Beauty supplies the final table.
short_description: Civic memory, bold art, stained glass and a fairy-tale pub finish.
author: Day Tripping Quiz
recommended_age: Recommended 10+; under-18s with an adult; check final venue policy
transport_note: A compact central route between Centenary Square, Victoria Square and Colmore Row.

before_you_go.terrain: Paved civic squares and city-centre streets, with broad pedestrian areas and busy central crossings.
before_you_go.hills: Gentle central-city gradients, with no sustained climb.
before_you_go.steps: The intended exterior route uses level approaches and does not require building entry.
before_you_go.accessibility: Broad public spaces make most of the route step-free, but events, tram works and crowding can alter routes.
before_you_go.toilets: Check current library, museum, shopping-centre and council facility listings before departure.
before_you_go.footwear: Comfortable shoes for hard city paving are recommended.
before_you_go.dogs: Outdoor route; keep dogs under control and check the finishing venue’s current dog policy before entering.
before_you_go.pushchairs: Generally easy on broad pavements, with temporary diversions the main variable.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Begin at the small domed hall built so a city's lost names would not fade.
stops.Hint_1: Head to Centenary Square beside the Library of Birmingham.
stops.Hint_2: Find the Portland-stone memorial hall with bronze figures outside.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The Hall of Memory opened in 1925 to commemorate Birmingham citizens killed in the First World War. It was designed by S. N. Cooke and W. N. Twist.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From the surrounding square, choose one exterior figure or inscription and note what it represents.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Seek the civic palace where industry paid for pictures and Pre-Raphaelite colours glow.
stops.Hint_1: Walk east through Victoria Square towards Chamberlain Square.
stops.Hint_2: Find the grand museum entrance beneath its clock-tower complex.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery opened in 1885. Its collection is especially noted for Pre-Raphaelite art, reflecting the city's links with artists and makers.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Without entering, identify one sculpture, mosaic or carved material on the exterior.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find a Baroque church whose windows bloom with work by a local master of colour.
stops.Hint_1: Continue east to the green space of Cathedral Square.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the compact cathedral dedicated to Saint Philip.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The church was completed in 1715 to designs by Thomas Archer and became Birmingham Cathedral in 1905. Its stained-glass windows include work by Birmingham-born Edward Burne-Jones.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From outside, find one round-headed window and compare it with the square's modern buildings.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Finish where Sleeping Beauty's thorny hedge remembers the artist born on this very hill.
stops.Hint_2: Find the food-serving pub and hotel with a fairy-tale flower in its name.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! The pub is named for Edward Burne-Jones's Briar Rose paintings on the Sleeping Beauty theme. Burne-Jones was born on Bennetts Hill in 1833. Check today's hours, then stop for food or a drink if it is open.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Find the flower or fairy-tale reference used on the frontage.
